paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Wirral, including Wirral Council's own fostering service. The council's fostering report for 2024-25, published in November 2025, counted 262 approved fostering households caring for more than 384 of the borough's children in care, and said more carers are still needed because recruitment is hard locally and nationally.

Wirral has tried practical ways to make room for more children. Its Extra Bedroom Scheme offers carers £500 for making another bedroom available, and had created seven new placements by the end of 2024-25; small grants for garage conversions had added four more by October 2025. The council also recruits through Foster4, a hub shared with other councils in Cheshire and Merseyside, backed by Department for Education funding that also paid for the Mockingbird programme.

Under Mockingbird, an experienced hub carer supports a small group of nearby foster families with advice, training, sleepovers and social time. Wirral's first group began in November 2024 and links six foster families. The council has also expanded mentoring and support groups for its carers.

You do not need a partner to foster: the council says around a third of its foster carers foster on their own, and some start with respite care before taking on a child full-time. Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before choosing, and see the Liverpool, Cheshire and Merseyside pages if you live near the borough's edge.
